items.title: Poll reveals Brampton is getting happier, Mississauga not so much
items.summary: “Don’t worry, be happy” may be the newest motto for Brampton, if a new national poll is any indication. The Leger survey ranks Brampton as the second-happiest of Canada’s 10 largest cities, with residents reporting a dramatic five-point increase in their happiness compared with last year. 7. 7 in 2025, the biggest year-over-year increase among the country’s 10 largest cities. That means Brampton has gone from fifth place among Canada’s biggest cities last year to second this year. So whatever residents may have been feeling in 2025, the latest numbers suggest they are feeling considerably better in 2026. And Brampton’s jump stands out even more when compared with some of its GTA neighbours. 7 and now sits sixth. 6.

items.title: Police allege Mississauga man arrived in Sudbury with cocaine and loaded handgun
items.summary: A Mississauga man is facing drug trafficking and firearms charges after police say he was arrested while entering Greater Sudbury with approximately $50,000 worth of cocaine and a loaded handgun. Greater Sudbury Police Service (GSPS) arrested 36-year-old Kmar Kelly on Aug. 23 following an investigation by the force’s Drug Enforcement Unit. Police say detectives, assisted by the Emergency Response Unit and Community Response Unit, arrested the man as he entered Greater Sudbury. Investigators then executed a search warrant at a downtown residence associated with the accused. The search turned up approximately 500 grams of cocaine, a loaded Ruger semi-automatic handgun, four cell phones and $3,000 in Canadian cash, according to police. The cocaine has an estimated street value of approximately $50,000. Police also seized another $500 in cash, digital scales, packaging materials and cutting agents during the search of the downtown residence. Kelly, who is from Mississauga, has been charged under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act and the Criminal Code with possession of a Schedule I substance for the purpose of trafficking, possession of property obtained by crime under $5,000, possession of a firearm knowing its possession is unauthorized, and possession of a prohibited or restricted firearm with ammunition.

items.title: As TIFF approaches, local filmmakers are ready to take the spotlight in Mississauga
items.summary: As the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) gets ready to turn the spotlight on movies from around the world, moviegoers in Mississauga may not have to travel downtown to find interesting films. Some of the most compelling stories are being made much closer to home. CreativeHub 1352 is bringing local filmmakers together this week for Made Here: A Night of Local Short Films, an evening showcasing three short films created by filmmakers from Mississauga and surrounding communities. The event takes place Thursday, Aug. 27, inside the historic Small Arms Inspection Building in Lakeview. The films offer very different perspectives, ranging from a family drama dealing with mental health and tragedy to a story about a man who has put his musical ambitions aside and a documentary-style exploration of identity and the pressures of everyday life. For CreativeHub 1352, the evening is about more than simply putting films on a screen. It is an opportunity to give local filmmakers an audience while introducing residents to creative voices that may be working right in their own neighbourhoods. , directed by Sabrina Narzoles Aly.

items.title: 3 highrises proposed for neighbourhood in Mississauga; residents and councillor say ‘no’
items.summary: Residents and their city councillor say they’re opposed to a proposed infill development that would add three 20-storey apartment buildings to an east Mississauga neighbourhood. The development is proposed for 4100 Ponytrail Dr. and 1850 Rathburn Rd. , on the border with the Etobicoke area of Toronto, and includes a total of 695 residential units split among the three highrises. Two 18-storey apartment buildings already exist on the site and approval was previously granted for construction of a third highrise, which will rise 25 storeys and house 283 units, according to the City of Mississauga. If the development is approved, it would increase the number of residential units at the site to 1,365. The proposal calls for 40 per cent of the units to be two bedrooms in size or larger. Chelsea on the Green is the applicant that submitted the development proposal to the city. Rendering shows aerial view of the proposed new buildings along with the existing buildings on the property. (Image: Submission to City of Mississauga) Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca said in an Aug. 11 letter to residents who had earlier reached out to her with concerns about the development that she agrees with their position. “Similar to many of you, while I support responsible growth, the scale of this proposal represents significant overdevelopment,” she wrote in the letter. “Adding multiple highrise towers to an already-dense site creates severe cumulative impacts on our traffic, local infrastructure and neighbourhood character.

6 new parks will take shape on waterfront in Mississauga over next several years
items.summary: Six new parks, including a $120-million destination pier, are being built as part of a huge mixed-use waterfront community in southeast Mississauga. Being developed by Lakeview Community Partners Limited, the 177-acre Lakeview Village includes numerous features and amenities that include a half dozen parks/public areas. Totalling nearly 46 acres, the parks are being developed in phases over the next six or so years, starting with Waterfront Park, according to a City of Mississauga online project update. Rendering of what a new Mississauga pier might look like. (Image: Lakeview Community Partners Limited) Expanding the Trans Canada Trail system is also part of the overall plan. The city received a $17 million grant from the Canadian government to expand active transportation — walking, cycling, rolling — along the major trail system. The initiative will connect the trail between Mississauga and Toronto, linking Lakefront Promenade Park in the west to the new Jim Tovey Lakeview Conservation Area in the east, officials said. Lakeview Village saw construction begin on the first homes in the community in summer 2025.

items.title: Mississauga’s Culham Trail secures $5.2M for flood-resilient upgrades
items.summary: 2-million federal investment will revamp Mississauga's Culham Trail to address recurring flood damage. Planned upgrades include raising the trail, strengthening riverbanks, and enhancing infrastructure to improve resilience and preserve this vital community space. Frequent flooding has significantly impacted the Culham Trail at Riverwood Conservancy in Mississauga, resulting in portions of the multi-use path being closed since 2024. 2-million federal investment to reconstruct nearly four kilometres of the popular trail, which is used by over 500,000 people annually. This initiative could offer a model for how municipalities can build more resilient infrastructure in the future A key focus of the reconstruction will involve elevating the trail to the five-year flood level to mitigate future flood damage. Reinforcements to riverbanks, improvements to boardwalks, and the addition of benches, signage and enhanced landscaping are also part of the project. “This investment will make the trail more resilient and accessible for the community,” said Joe Horneck, Mississauga Ward 6 Councillor. 8-million federal initiative to improve active transportation infrastructure across Mississauga.

items.title: $95,000 Grant Will Train Youth Ambassadors to Fight Islamophobia in Brampton and Mississauga
items.summary: According to INsauga, a new Safe Voices Peel initiative aimed at combating Islamophobia in Brampton and Mississauga has received more than $95,000 in funding from the province of Ontario. The outlet reports Zee Hamid, the MPP for Milton, announced Wednesday that $95,100 would go to Building Multicultural Communities through the province's Safer and Vital Communities Grant. INsauga reports the money will support a program that trains youth ambassadors in hate crime prevention, community safety and bystander intervention, with the initiative running in both cities. According to the outlet, organizers are partnering with Peel Regional Police, Brampton Library, Our Place Peel and other local community groups to deliver the program. Hamid said building safer communities starts at the grassroots level, according to INsauga. The outlet reports the initiative is expected to bring youth and community organizations together to raise awareness about hate prevention and encourage residents to take an active role in creating safer, more inclusive neighbourhoods.

items.title: TK Ultra Lounge Among Four Mississauga Businesses Handed Conditional Health Passes
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Peel Public Health issued conditional passes to three Mississauga restaurants and a medical esthetics spa following recent inspections. The outlet reports Peel Public Health inspectors routinely check restaurants, cocktail bars, beverage rooms, bakeries, takeout establishments and other businesses to ensure they meet food and personal service safety standards. Mississauga.com reports TK Ultra Lounge, a restaurant at 1 Derry Road, was among the businesses inspected, with its inspection taking place on August 25. According to the outlet, a green pass indicates a business is meeting requirements under Ontario's Health Protection and Promotion Act, while a conditional pass signals violations inspectors found during a visit. Mississauga.com notes the routine inspection program gives residents a way to check the food and personal-service safety record of local businesses.

items.title: Child E-Scooter Injuries Jump 29 Per Cent at Mississauga Hospitals This Spring
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, two Mississauga hospitals recorded a 29 per cent jump in e-scooter-related emergency room visits this spring compared with the same period last year, with children under 18 making up a growing share of the cases. The outlet reports Credit Valley Hospital and Mississauga Hospital logged 134 emergency department visits tied to e-scooter injuries between April and June, according to data Trillium Health Partners provided to the publication, up 30 visits from the same three months in 2025. Mississauga.com reports children under 18 accounted for 65 per cent of those visits, compared with 49 per cent during the same stretch a year earlier. The outlet notes e-scooters are legal in Mississauga, but enforcement of e-scooter and e-bike violations falls to Peel Regional Police rather than the city. According to Mississauga.com, the Canadian Paediatric Surveillance Program's newly published 2025 results identified 57 severe e-scooter and e-bike injury cases among children and youth nationwide. The outlet frames the local numbers as part of a broader pattern of underage riding and enforcement gaps playing out across the city.

items.title: Nearly 500 Newcomers Have Taken Mississauga's Free Water Safety Course Since 2024
items.summary: According to INsauga, the City of Mississauga says nearly 500 people who have moved to Canada within the past five years have enrolled in its free Swim to Survive program for newcomers since the initiative launched in summer 2024. INsauga reports the program, delivered through the Lifesaving Society, is aimed at preventing drowning and water-related injuries by teaching what city officials call the essential skills every Canadian should know in a water emergency. According to the outlet, the free program is open to newcomers ages eight and older and consists of three one-hour classes covering how to roll into deep water, tread water for one minute and swim 50 metres. City officials told INsauga the program addresses a critical but often overlooked aspect of settlement in water safety as Mississauga continues to welcome new residents. INsauga notes the program's popularity reflects a broader push by the city to make water safety education accessible to newcomer families.

items.title: Windsor Arrest Near U.S. Border Leads to Murder Charges in 2022 Toronto Studio Shooting
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto police say a Mississauga man has been charged with two counts of second-degree murder and one count of attempted murder in connection with a 2022 shooting inside a music studio in west Toronto. INsauga reports the suspect, 25-year-old Darriel Thompson, was arrested by Windsor police on August 22 near the U.S. border and was scheduled to appear in a Toronto court the day the charges were announced. The outlet reports the shooting killed Minyali Wur, 24, and Chudier Reat, 20, both of Mississauga, on January 3, 2022, at a studio on Thirtieth Street just east of the Mississauga border. According to INsauga, police also found an injured woman at the scene that night, and all three victims were taken to hospital, where the two Mississauga men later died of their injuries while the woman survived. INsauga notes the studio's address also housed offices and apartments in the same building.
